Square $ EFGH$ is inside the square $ ABCD$ so that each side of $ EFGH$ can be extended to pass through a vertex of $ ABCD$. Square $ ABCD$ has side length $ \sqrt{50}$ and $ BE = 1$. What is the area of the inner square $ EFGH$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the figure: In the outer square ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the upper right, C is at the lower right, and D is at the lower left. The inner square EFGH is placed tilted; the extension of the line on which side HE lies passes through B, the extension of the line on which side EF lies passes through C, the extension of the line on which side FG lies passes through D, and the extension of the line on which side GH lies passes through A. The problem gives the side length of the outer square as s=√50, and BE=1. Then reason: establish a coordinate system according to the specified method, let D=(0,0), C=(s,0), B=(s,s), A=(0,s), where s=√50. Because BE=1, let the unit vector from B to E be (-p,-q), then p^2+q^2=1, and E=(s-p,s-q). Side EF is perpendicular to BE, so the direction vector from E toward C can be taken as (q,-p). Since C is on the extension of EF, let C-E=λ(q,-p). Thus (s,0)-(s-p,s-q)=(p,q-s)=λ(q,-p), so p=λq, q-s=-λp. From λ=p/q, get q-s=-p^2/q, that is q^2-sq=-p^2, so p^2+q^2=sq. Also p^2+q^2=1, therefore sq=1, q=1/s. Thus p^2=1-1/s^2=1-1/50=49/50, so p=7/s, and λ=p/q=7. Let the side length EF of the inner square be x. Then F=E+x(q,-p). Substitute E=(s-p,s-q), p=7/s, q=1/s, s^2=50, obtaining E=(43/s,49/s), so F=((43+x)/s,(49-7x)/s). On the other hand, D is on the extension of FG, and FG is parallel to BE, so F is on the ray starting from D in the direction (p,q), hence F=(νp,νq)=(7ν/s,ν/s). Comparing coordinates gives 7ν=43+x, ν=49-7x. Therefore (43+x)/7=49-7x, solving gives 43+x=343-49x, 50x=300, x=6. The area of the inner square is x^2=36.

method.method_draft: Use a geometric rotation/congruence argument. From the image, triangle BEC is a right triangle: BE lies along the extension of side EH, EC lies along the extension of side EF, and EH ⟂ EF. Its hypotenuse is BC, a side of the outer square. Because ABCD is a square, rotating side BC by 90° gives side CD; because EFGH is also a square, the two inner-side directions also rotate by 90°. Therefore the adjacent right triangle at C, namely triangle CFD, has corresponding leg CF equal to BE. Repeating around the square shows the small outside segments are all equal, so CF=BE=1. Now in right triangle BEC, the hypotenuse BC has length √50 and one leg BE has length 1, so EC=√(50-1)=7. Since EC consists of EF plus CF, the inner side length is EF=7-1=6. Thus the area of square EFGH is 6^2=36.

Because BE=1, let the unit vector from B to E be (-p,-q), then p^2+q^2=1, and E=(s-p,s-q). Side EF is perpendicular to BE, so the direction vector from E toward C can be taken as (q,-p). Since C is on the extension of EF, let C-E=λ(q,-p). Thus (s,0)-(s-p,s-q)=(p,q-s)=λ(q,-p), so p=λq, q-s=-λp. From λ=p/q, get q-s=-p^2/q, that is q^2-sq=-p^2, so p^2+q^2=sq. Also p^2+q^2=1, therefore sq=1, q=1/s. Thus p^2=1-1/s^2=1-1/50=49/50, so p=7/s, and λ=p/q=7.

Let the side length EF of the inner square be x. Then F=E+x(q,-p). Substitute E=(s-p,s-q), p=7/s, q=1/s, s^2=50, obtaining E=(43/s,49/s), so F=((43+x)/s,(49-7x)/s). On the other hand, D is on the extension of FG, and FG is parallel to BE, so F is on the ray starting from D in the direction (p,q), hence F=(νp,νq)=(7ν/s,ν/s). Comparing coordinates gives 7ν=43+x, ν=49-7x. Therefore (43+x)/7=49-7x, solving gives 43+x=343-49x, 50x=300, x=6. The area of the inner square is x^2=36.
